prompt: Why does the course teach SAP, Dynamics and Salesforce from documentation rather than having you use them?
hint: Think about who they are sold to.

choices.text: They are too old to run on a current computer
choices.why: They run today in thousands of companies; age is not the obstacle.

choices.text: They are sold to companies under enterprise contracts, not to a person
choices.why: Right: there is no bill an individual can pay for a licence, so the course designs around that.

choices.text: Their vendors forbid anyone from describing them in a course
choices.why: Their documentation is published, which is exactly what the lessons are built from.

choices.text: Using one would teach configuration, which architects leave to consultants
choices.why: The reason is access, not a judgement about configuration; architects do need to understand it.

prompt: Salesforce offers a free Developer Edition org. Why does the course still not depend on it?
hint: What happens to the course if the offer changes?

choices.text: A Developer Edition org has none of the standard objects the lesson describes
choices.why: It is a real org with the standard objects; that is not the reason.

choices.text: Free offers are only for students of Salesforce's own training
choices.why: Anybody can sign up; the problem is depending on it at all.

choices.text: A course that needs one company's offer breaks when the offer changes
choices.why: Right: the lessons name it where it helps and work without it.

prompt: What makes a set of business programs an ERP, by the lesson's definition?
hint: Follow the truck of yoghurt leaving the plant.

choices.text: It includes an accounting module
choices.why: Accounting packages existed long before ERPs; one module does not make the whole.

choices.text: It is sold by one of the large vendors, such as SAP or Oracle
choices.why: TOTVS, Odoo and ERPNext are ERPs too; the vendor is not the definition.

choices.text: It has a screen for every department in the company
choices.why: The screens are the least interesting part, the lesson says.

choices.text: Its functions share one data model and one database
choices.why: Right: stock, cost, receivable and plan change in one transaction.

prompt: Put these in the order they appeared.
hint: Material first, then the factory, then the enterprise.
items: MRP: what to buy and when, from the plan and the bill of materials
MRP II: machine capacity, labour and money added
ERP: sales, finance, purchasing and personnel on one database
SAP R/3 released, the product most people picture

prompt: Why is each of Serra Alta's 1,900 farms a vendor master record in SAP?
hint: What does the ERP need to know about a farm?

choices.text: Serra Alta buys their milk and pays them, as it pays any supplier
choices.why: Right: the ERP has no concept of a farm, only of somebody Serra Alta pays.

choices.text: Coleta created them that way in 1996, and nobody has changed it
choices.why: Coleta is outside SAP; the record type comes from SAP's own model.

choices.text: The tax authority requires farms to be registered as companies
choices.why: Many farms are people with a CPF; the reason is the payment, not their legal form.

choices.text: SAP's production module treats raw milk as a material from a plant
choices.why: Milk is a material, but the farm that sells it is a vendor, which is what gets paid.

prompt: A vendor says its standard process is close to best practice. What does the lesson say about that claim?
hint: Accounting is accounting.

choices.text: It is marketing, and a company should customise every process to its own way
choices.why: That ignores the half that is true, and the cost of customising is the subject of the last section.

choices.text: Partly true; tell the standard parts from the company's own
choices.why: Right: nobody competes on recording a receivable, and the parts that are a company's own rarely fit.

choices.text: True, which is why companies adopt the standard and stop thinking about it
choices.why: The parts of a business that are how it competes rarely fit any standard.

prompt: Match each SAP module to what it records at Serra Alta.
hint: The letters are abbreviations of English names.

pairs.right: the laboratory results of each batch
the weekly plan of each plant

prompt: In the 1990s, sales, stock and accounting each gave a true but different answer to "what did we sell in March". Why?
hint: Each copy was correct by its own rules.

choices.text: The nightly files between the three systems lost records on the way
choices.why: Late or lost files made it worse, but the lesson says the differences were not carelessness.

choices.text: Each system counted a sale at a different moment
choices.why: Right: three databases with three rules give three true answers.

choices.text: People typed the same customers differently in each of the three systems
choices.why: Duplicated master data caused trouble, but not three different sales totals.

prompt: Sort each item into master data or transactional data.
hint: Does it describe a thing, or record that something happened?

prompt: The stock table says 840 cases are in the Juiz de Fora cold store. Why is that not the number to promise a bakery?
hint: Where does the meaning live?

choices.text: The table is updated only once a night, so it is a day old
choices.why: Inside the ERP the table is current; the problem is what it leaves out.

choices.text: Cases in a cold store belong to Mantiqueira's ERP
choices.why: Juiz de Fora is Serra Alta's own plant, in SAP.

choices.text: Promisable stock is computed in SAP's code, not stored
choices.why: Right: reservations, quality blocks and stock in transit are a calculation, and reading the row skips it.

choices.text: Physical stock is kept in a separate database for the warehouse
choices.why: The point of the ERP is that it is not: one database holds it.

prompt: `design-patterns` warned against one model for a whole company. Why does an ERP get away with it?
hint: Who agreed on the words, and over how long?

choices.text: It does not: an ERP is several bounded contexts with separate databases
choices.why: The modules share one database on purpose; that is the definition the lesson gives.

choices.text: Decades of accounting practice settled what most of its words mean
choices.why: Right: and where a company's own words differ, somebody loses the argument.

choices.text: Its vendor rewrites the model for every customer during the implementation
choices.why: Customers configure the vendor's model; nobody rewrites it per customer.

choices.text: Bounded contexts only apply to software built as microservices
choices.why: They are about models and language, whatever the deployment.

prompt: In SAP ECC, customer master data sits in tables such as `KNA1`, and sales order items in `___`.
hint: Four characters, V for Vertrieb.

prompt: Put the documents of an order-to-cash chain in the order SAP creates them.
hint: Nothing changes the books until the truck is loaded.

prompt: A goods issue was posted to the wrong plant. How is it put right?
hint: An auditor has to see what happened.

choices.text: Edit the plant on the posted document
choices.why: A posted document is final; editing it would let anybody change what the books say happened.

choices.text: Delete it and post it again, so the books show one clean entry
choices.why: Deleting hides the mistake from the auditor, which is the thing the design prevents.

choices.text: Reverse it with a new document, then post it again to the right plant
choices.why: Right: all three documents stay in the books.

prompt: Which step in the order-to-cash chain is the first to change the books?
hint: Stock and cost move together.

choices.text: The sales order, because the customer has committed to buy
choices.why: Nothing has moved and nothing is owed at the order.

choices.text: The goods issue
choices.why: Right: stock falls and the cost moves to cost of goods sold when the truck is loaded.

choices.text: The billing document, because the NF-e is the legal record of the sale
choices.why: The invoice creates the receivable, after the goods issue has already moved stock and cost.

choices.text: The outbound delivery, because the warehouse has started picking
choices.why: A delivery is an instruction to prepare; it posts nothing.

prompt: Bakeries pay by card on the Portal B2B. A developer proposes creating the invoice in SAP directly, since payment is already done. What goes wrong?
hint: What does an invoice point at?

choices.text: Nothing, as long as the portal sends the right amount and tax
choices.why: Amount and tax are right and the stock is still never issued.

choices.text: SAP refuses an invoice for a customer with no credit check
choices.why: The bigger problem is silent: the invoice is accepted and points at no delivery.

choices.text: No delivery exists, so stock never leaves the books
choices.why: Right: enter the chain as a sales order and let SAP create the rest.

prompt: Rota needs to know when an order has shipped. What should it ask SAP about?
hint: A summary versus the event.

choices.text: The status field on the sales order
choices.why: The status is a summary SAP computes for its own screens.

choices.text: The incoming payment, because shipment is only final once the money arrives
choices.why: Payment comes thirty days after shipping; it answers a different question.

choices.text: The goods issue
choices.why: Right: it is the event, posted when the truck is loaded.

choices.text: The stock table, comparing it before and after
choices.why: That is reading the tables, and the stock changes for many reasons besides one order.

prompt: What was the first of Edson's four objections to letting the portal query SAP's stock tables on a replica?
hint: MATDOC.

choices.text: The tables are SAP's private structure, and they change in the move to S/4HANA
choices.why: Right: a table you can read is not a table designed to be read by you.

choices.text: A replica would put too much load on the production database
choices.why: The replica exists to avoid that load; it was the part of the proposal that worked.

choices.text: The portal is written in a language that cannot connect to SAP's database
choices.why: Any language can connect to a database; the objections were about meaning and ownership.

prompt: What did the High Court decide in SAP v Diageo (2017)?
hint: Indirect access.

choices.text: That reading SAP's tables directly from another system breaches copyright
choices.why: The case was about licences for users of other systems, not copyright in tables.

choices.text: That companies may connect any system to SAP without extra cost
choices.why: The court found the opposite, in SAP's favour.

choices.text: That users of systems reading SAP data needed SAP licences
choices.why: Right: and that is why a design that puts 4,000 bakeries in front of SAP data starts with the contract.

choices.text: That Diageo had to move its customer systems off Salesforce and into SAP
choices.why: The ruling was about licences owed, not where the systems had to run.

prompt: Which of the three places to put a change is broken by every upgrade of the ERP?
hint: Whose code is it, and where does it sit?

choices.text: Configuration
choices.why: The vendor built those choices and carries them through its upgrades.

choices.text: An extension beside the ERP, talking through published interfaces
choices.why: It is yours to maintain, but the vendor's release does not break it.

choices.text: A modification: your own code changed inside the vendor's programs
choices.why: Right: it has to be found, tested and carried forward every time.

prompt: The portal now calls an SAP service for available-to-promise. It is 01:30 on a Sunday. What should it do?
hint: SAP is down until 05:00.

choices.text: Show the last figure and the time it was taken; confirm orders later
choices.why: Right: the ERP's window is a constraint the portal designs for, not an outage it suffers.

choices.text: Close the ordering pages until SAP comes back at 05:00
choices.why: Bakeries order before they open; closing turns a known window into lost orders.

choices.text: Fall back to reading the stock tables on the replica for those four hours
choices.why: The replica follows the primary and is down with it, and its numbers were wrong anyway.

choices.text: Treat every product as available and sort out shortages on Monday
choices.why: That is the forty-minute problem made worse, with customer service calling back more bakeries.

prompt: Changing the business process to fit what the ERP does out of the box, instead of changing the ERP, is what the vendors call fit to ___.
hint: The opposite of custom.

prompt: Rota wants the list of deliveries for tomorrow. Which design respects every line of Joana's table?
hint: Doors, documents, calendar.

choices.text: A nightly query on SAP's delivery tables, since it only reads
choices.why: Reading the tables couples Rota to SAP's private structure, and reading is still indirect use.

choices.text: A published SAP interface, with Sunday's window planned
choices.why: Right: a published door, the delivery document as the event, and the calendar designed in.

choices.text: A custom ABAP report added inside SAP that writes a file for Rota
choices.why: Code inside the ERP is carried through every upgrade; prefer an extension beside it.

prompt: Which of these does the ERP decide for the systems around it, by the lesson's table? Choose all that apply.
hint: Four of the five.

choices.text: Which day the month is closed
choices.why: Right: its close is everybody's calendar.

choices.text: What a customer is, as a record
choices.why: Right: its data model supplies the meanings.

choices.text: Which programming language the portal is written in
choices.why: The ERP constrains how the portal enters, not what it is built with.

choices.text: Who may read its data, through the licence
choices.why: Right: that is in a contract.

choices.text: The step at which an outside system joins a business process
choices.why: Right: the document flow sets it.

prompt: Joana's decision record starts with "SAP is the system of record for stock; the portal does not read its tables." Why lead with that rather than with the service and the cache?
hint: Which of the two outlives the other?

choices.text: Decision records must start with a rule, by the ADR template
choices.why: No template requires it; the reason is what the sentence protects.

choices.text: Because the service and the cache were Edson's idea, not hers
choices.why: Authorship is not the point; the record is about the reasoning.

choices.text: So that finance can read it without technical vocabulary
choices.why: Finance may read it, but that is a side effect of naming the constraint.

choices.text: The constraint stays true after the technology around it has changed
choices.why: Right: the service may be replaced; the reason for it will not be.
